## Findings
- claim-1: For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the two sets \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},\qquad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\} \] generate \(J_v\subseteq H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\); each has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The paper conjectures that both sets are minimal and reports computer verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1489-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: The paper applies its graded proposition with \(\Lambda\) the graded ring of symmetric functions over \(\mathbb Z\), \(M=J_v\), and explicitly leaves unresolved whether \(M/\Lambda_+M\) requires \(N\) generators or is \(\mathbb Z^N\). [source-2@L1517-L1552|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: **Indexed graded Nakayama.** Let \(R\) be commutative unital, \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{e\ge0}\Lambda_e\) a connected graded \(R\)-algebra with \(\Lambda_0=R\), and \(M=\bigoplus_{d\ge d_0}M_d\) a bounded-below graded \(\Lambda\)-module. For any indexed homogeneous family \((m_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}\), it generates \(M\) iff \((\bar m_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}\) spans \(Q:=M/\Lambda_+M\) over \(R\). Indeed, the forward direction is immediate. Conversely, induct on \(d\). For \(x\in M_d\), gradedness gives \[ x-\sum_{\alpha\in F,\ \deg m_\alpha=d}r_\alpha m_\alpha\in(\Lambda_+M)_d =\sum_{e>0}\Lambda_eM_{d-e}, \] for a finite \(F\subset A\). Every latter module factor has degree \(<d\), hence belongs to the generated submodule by induction.
- claim-5: Under the hypotheses above, the family \((m_\alpha)\) is inclusion-minimal precisely when \((\bar m_\alpha)\) is an inclusion-minimal \(R\)-spanning family of \(Q\): apply indexed graded Nakayama to every subfamily obtained by deleting one index.
- claim-6: If \(A=\Lambda/I\), \(J\subseteq A\) is an ideal, and \(S\subseteq J\), then \(S\) generates \(J\) as an \(A\)-ideal iff it generates \(J\) as a \(\Lambda\)-module. Thus the preceding criterion applies to \(J_v\).
- claim-7: An exact sufficient hypothesis for either displayed \(N\)-element Schur family to be irredundant is \[ \mu_{\mathbb Z}\!\left(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\right)=N. \] It spans the quotient by graded Nakayama; deletion would give a spanning family of \(N-1\) elements, contradicting the hypothesis.
- claim-8: A stronger sufficient hypothesis is \[ J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^N. \] An \(N\)-element spanning family of \(\mathbb Z^N\) cannot remain spanning after a deletion, since \(\mathbb Z^{N-1}\) cannot surject onto \(\mathbb Z^N\).
- claim-9: **Free-summand irredundance construction.** If \(R\ne0\), \(Q=R^d\oplus T\), and \(t_1,\ldots,t_k\) is an inclusion-minimal spanning family of \(T\), then \[ \{(e_\ell,0):1\le\ell\le d\}\ \cup\ \{(0,t_j):1\le j\le k\} \] is an inclusion-minimal spanning family of \(Q\). Coordinate projections witness necessity of the first \(d\) elements, and \(Q\to T\) witnesses necessity of the others.
- claim-10: **CRT-aligned construction.** Let \(n_1,\ldots,n_k>1\) be pairwise coprime, \(M=\prod_i n_i\), and \(T=\mathbb Z/M\). Choose \(c_i\) with \(c_i(M/n_i)\equiv1\pmod {n_i}\), and put \(\epsilon_i=c_iM/n_i\bmod M\). Under \[ T\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^k\mathbb Z/n_i, \] \(\epsilon_i\) is the \(i\)-th coordinate unit. Hence \(\{\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_k\}\) is inclusion-minimal spanning, while \(\{1\}\) is also inclusion-minimal spanning.
- claim-11: Claim 9 is correct: in \(\mathbb Z/6\), \(\{1\}\) generates, while \(\{2,3\}\) generates because \(1=2\cdot2-3\), and neither singleton \(\{2\}\) nor \(\{3\}\) generates. Thus both are inclusion-minimal, of cardinalities \(1\) and \(2\). More generally, adjoining the free summand \(\mathbb Z^d\) to the CRT construction gives irredundant spanning families of \(\mathbb Z^d\oplus\mathbb Z/M\) of sizes \(d+1\) and \(d+k\).
- claim-12: No supplied evidence proves \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)=\binom{a+b}{a}\), torsion-freeness of this quotient, or the source’s stronger \(\mathbb Z^N\) formulation; consequently the minimality conjecture for \(J_v\) remains unresolved.
## Strategy
- Apply indexed graded Nakayama to \(Q=M/\Lambda_+M\): since \(Q\) is graded, a degree-\(d\) class is spanned using only images of degree-\(d\) family members. Strong induction on \(d\), vacuous below the lower degree bound, proves generation upstairs iff spanning downstairs.
- Thus an indexed homogeneous family is inclusion-minimal iff its image is an inclusion-minimal \(\mathbb Z\)-spanning family of \(Q\), including families with repeated values.
- For \(J_v\), the source-backed Schur families each have \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) homogeneous generators. The sufficient numerical hypothesis
  \[
  \mu_{\mathbb Z}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)=N
  \]
  makes each irredundant. The exact criterion remains minimality of its image spanning family in \(Q\).
- Record explicit non-common-cardinality constructions. If \(R\ne0\), \(T\) is an \(R\)-module, and \(t_1,\dots,t_k\) is irredundant spanning in \(T\), then
  \[
  \{(e_\ell,0)\}_{\ell=1}^d\cup\{(0,t_j)\}_{j=1}^k
  \]
  is irredundant spanning in \(R^d\oplus T\). Coordinate and \(T\)-projections witness necessity.
- For \(1\le k<\infty\), pairwise coprime \(n_i>1\), \(M=\prod_i n_i\), and
  \[
  \epsilon_i=c_iM/n_i\pmod M,\qquad c_i(M/n_i)\equiv1\pmod {n_i},
  \]
  CRT identifies \(\{\epsilon_i\}\) with coordinate units in \(\mathbb Z/M\cong\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z/n_i\). Hence it is irredundant, whereas \(\{1\}\) is also irredundant. For \(k\ge2\), adjoining \(\mathbb Z^d\) gives irredundant families of sizes \(d+1\) and \(d+k\).

## Gaps
- Neither construction proves
  \[
  \mu_{\mathbb Z}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)=N
  \quad\text{or}\quad
  J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^N.
  \]
  The \(J_v\) minimality conjecture remains unresolved.
- Graded Nakayama over \(\mathbb Z\) does not imply that all inclusion-minimal generating families have common cardinality: \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2,3\}\) are irredundant spanning families of \(\mathbb Z/6\).
- The free-summand and CRT examples are abstract module constructions and provide no decomposition or lower bound for the actual indecomposables of \(J_v\).

## Next
- Obtain an integral presentation of \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) and compute Smith normal form, or establish matching lower bounds modulo every relevant prime.
- Separately prove torsion-freeness if the stronger free-\(\mathbb Z^N\) statement is sought.
- Do not infer a common cardinality for arbitrary minimal generating sets from the graded Nakayama criterion.
